Q1: Which plans should the new gate hold back from automatic `/approved` while `AUTOMATION_PATH_PLAN_AUTO_APPROVAL_ENABLED` is off (the default)?
Choices:
A: Every plan, whatever files it touches. Auto-approval stops repo-wide until someone sets the flag to `true`.
B: Only plans whose planned files include automation paths (`.github/`, `.claude/`, `scripts/`, `prompts/`, `workflow-templates/`). Other plans keep today's `AUTO_IMPLEMENT_ON_CLEAR_PLAN` behaviour. When the flag is `true`, the fail-closed gate checks those paths against the issue's trusted exact `files_touched` grant: an ungranted plan (for example, a security finding) is held, with the missing protected paths reported in an `AI_PHASE_GATE_V1` line; a fully granted plan is approved automatically. (RECOMMENDED)
C: The flag only turns the grant check on or off. While it is off, behaviour stays exactly as it is today, with no suppression.
**Note:** A conflicts with the "granted plan" regression the issue asks for, because nothing is ever approved automatically under A while the flag is off.
Q2: Which branch should this change target?
Choices:
A: `main` only. `stable` gets the guard and this gate through the normal promote / release path, with no separate backport PR. (RECOMMENDED)
B: `main`, plus a separate backport PR that brings the existing guard (`files_touched_scope_guard.py` automation-path functions) and this gate to `stable`.
C: `stable` only, with "Target branch: stable", matching the original #6766 target.
Q3: Besides the `plan.yml` auto-approve step and the managed and standalone stall-recovery `auto_approve` actions in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`, should the gate also cover the staged-support latch release that posts `/approved [auto-approved-by-plan]`?
Choices:
A: Yes, put that release path behind the same gate too.
B: No. Limit the change to `plan.yml` and the two stall-recovery `auto_approve` paths. The latch release only re-approves a plan that was already approved and only runs in this source repo. (RECOMMENDED)
